==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|loc.||abbreviation}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*stel-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|local}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|locālis|t=belonging to a place}}, possibly also via {{der|en|fro|local}}; ultimately from {{der|en|la|locus|t=a place}}.

The {{l|en|local|id=ring|ring-theoretic senses}} derive from {{w|Wolfgang Krull|Krull}}, who first referred to Noetherian commutative rings with a unique maximal ideal as "Stellenring" ({{compound|de|Stellen|ring|t1=place|nocat=1}}) in 1938.<ref>Krull, Wolfgang. "Dimensionstheorie in Stellenringen [47]". Volume 1+2, edited by Paulo Ribenboim, Berlin, Boston: De Gruyter, 1999, pp. 730-734. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783110801026.730</ref> The term was inspired by [[algebraic geometry]], where local rings encode information about the behavior of curves (surfaces, etc.) at points; hence, describe "local" behavior.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈləʊ.kl̩/|a=RP}}
* {{enPR|lōk′əl|a=GenAm}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈloʊ.kl̩/}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-local.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|əʊkəl|s=2}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# From or in a nearby [[location]].
#: {{holonyms|en|statal|national|federal|unional|supranational|global}}
#: {{ux|en|We prefer '''local''' produce.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=XLIV|page=361|passage=Not unnaturally, “Auntie” took this communication in bad part.{{...}}Next day she{{...}}tried to recover her ward by the hair of the head. Then, thwarted, the wretched creature went to the police for help; she was versed in the law, and perhaps had spared no pains to keep on good terms with the '''local''' constabulary.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2012-12-01|volume=405|issue=8813|page=3 (Technology Quarterly)|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21567193-networking-enthusiasts-dream-building-drone-powered-internet-carry-objects An internet of airborne things]
|passage=A farmer could place an order for a new tractor part by text message and pay for it by mobile money-transfer. A supplier many miles away would then take the part to the '''local''' matternet station for airborne dispatch via drone.}}
# {{lb|en|computing|of a [[resource]]}} [[connect|Connect]]ed [[direct]]ly to a particular [[computer]], [[processor]], etc.; able to be [[access]]ed [[offline]].
#: {{ant|en|remote}}
#: {{co|en|'''local''' disk drive}}
#: {{co|en|'''local''' file}}
#: {{ux|en|The panel shows both '''local''' and remote sites.}}
# {{lb|en|computing|of a [[variable]] or [[identifier]]}} Having limited [[scope]] (either [[lexical]] or [[dynamic]]); only accessible within a certain portion of a [[program]].
#: {{ant|en|global}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics|not comparable|of a condition or property}} Applying to or satisfied by substructures understood as "near points;" in particular:
## {{lb|en|topology}} Satisfied by at least one [[open]] [[neighborhood]] of every point.
##: {{ux|en|A Hausdorff space satisfying '''local''' compactness need not be (globally) compact!}}
## {{lb|en|topology}} Satisfied by [[arbitrarily]] small open neighborhoods of every point.
## {{lb|en|group theory|of a property of an infinite group}} Satisfied by every finitely generated subgroup.
# {{lb|en|mathematics|not comparable|of a condition or property}} [[detectable|Detectable]] from the behavior of substructures understood to be "near points;" in particular:
## {{lb|en|algebra|algebraic geometry|of a property <math>P</math> of a [[ring]] <math>R</math> (or an <math>R</math>-[[module]] <math>M</math>)}} Such that the following conditions are equivalent: (1) <math>P</math> holds for <math>R</math> (<math>M</math>); (2) <math>P</math> holds for the [[localization]] <math>R_\mathfrak{p}</math> (<math>M_\mathfrak{p}</math>) for all [[prime ideal]]s <math>\mathfrak{p}</math> of <math>R</math>; (3) <math>P</math> holds for the localization <math>R_\mathfrak{m}</math> (<math>M_\mathfrak{m}</math>) for all [[maximal ideal]]s <math>\mathfrak{m}</math> of <math>R</math>.
##: {{ux|en|{{w|Flat module|Flatness}} is a '''local''' property.}}
## {{lb|en|group theory|of a property of a finite group}} Detectable from the behavior of the [[normalizer]]s of the nontrivial {{w|p-group|p-subgroups}}.
# {{senseid|en|ring}}{{lb|en|algebra|of a ring}} Having a unique maximal (left) ideal.
# {{lb|en|medicine}} Of or pertaining to a restricted part of an [[organism]].
#: {{syn|en|topical}}
#: {{co|en|'''local''' lesion}}
#: {{ux|en|The patient didn't want to be sedated, so we applied only '''local''' anesthesia.}}
# Descended from an indigenous population.
#: {{ux|en|Hawaiian Pidgin is spoken by the '''local''' population.}}
# {{lb|en|quantum mechanics}} Exhibiting or pertaining to [[locality]] {{gloss|adhering to the principle of locality}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A person who lives in or near a given place.
#: {{ux|en|It's easy to tell the '''locals''' from the tourists.}}
# A branch of a nationwide organization such as a [[trade union]].
#: {{ux|en|I'm in the TWU, too. '''Local''' 6.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=4 Feb 90|volume=17|number=29|journal=Gay Community News|page=18|author=Pam Mitchell|title=Pro-Union And Queer|text=Citing the risk involved with being out as a gay person ''and'' a union activist while simultaneously dealing with racism, Susan notes that there are no out gays or lesbians of color in her '''local''', though its membership is about 80 percent people of color.}}
# {{lb|en|rail transport}} {{clipping of|en|local train}}.
#: {{syn|en|stopper}}
#: {{ant|en|fast|express}}
#: {{ux|en|The expresses skipped my station, so I had to take a '''local'''.}}
# {{lb|en|British}} One's nearest or regularly frequented [[public house]] or [[bar]].
#: {{ux|en|I got barred from my '''local''', so I've started going all the way into town for a drink.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|year=2010|artist=The Script|album=Science & Faith|title={{w|Nothing (The Script song)|Nothing}}|passage=As they take me to my '''local''' down the street.}}
# {{lb|en|programming}} A [[locally]] [[scope]]d [[identifier]].
#: {{ux|en|Functional programming languages usually don't allow changing the immediate value of '''locals''' once they've been initialized, unless they're explicitly marked as being mutable.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Cesar Otero; Rob Larsen|title=Professional jQuery|page=25
|passage=Globals are visible anywhere in your application, whereas '''locals''' are visible only in the function in which they're declared.}}
# {{lb|en|US|slang|journalism}} An item of [[news]] relating to the place where the [[newspaper]] is published.<!--Webster 1913-->
# {{lb|en|colloquial|medicine}} {{clipping of|en|local anesthetic}}.
# {{lb|en|finance}} An [[independent]] [[trader]] who acts for themselves rather than on behalf of [[investor]]s.
#: {{syn|en|floor trader}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=R. Stafford Johnson|title=Bond Evaluation, Selection, and Management|page=316
|passage=On most futures exchanges, there are two major types of futures traders/members: commission brokers and '''locals'''.}}
# {{lb|en|fandom slang|derogatory}} A [[Twitter]] user who is not a part of [[Stan Twitter]].
#*: Her camera roll is filled with pictures and videos of her idol, she doesn't let any of her friends see her account because "no '''locals''' allowed", {{...}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=16 October 2018|author=Fergal Smiddy|title=The 6 Types of People You Meet on Twitter|journal=University Express|publisher=University College Cork, Ireland|pageurl=https://issuu.com/uccexpress/docs/cu2018-10-16iss3/11|page=11
|passage='''Locals''' are characterised by their seeming lack of involvement or ~expertise~ on the platform.}}
#* {{see more citations|en}}
